record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can nondeterminism be used together with catalytic computation in a genuinely nontrivial way, rather than merely by definition?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Utilize non-determinism in conjunction with catalytic computing in a non-trivial way.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A catalytic Turing machine is a space-bounded Turing machine equipped with three tapes: a read-only input tape, a work tape of size s(n) which is initially blank, and a catalytic (auxiliary) tape of size c(n) which is initialized with an arbitrary string τ. The machine may read and write freely on the catalytic tape during the computation, but is required to restore the catalytic tape to its original content τ by the end of every computation, for every initial τ. The class CSPACE[s(n), c(n)] consists of languages decided by such deterministic machines; the catalytic logspace class CL is defined by s(n) = O(log n) and c(n) = poly(n). A nondeterministic catalytic Turing machine is defined analogously, but the transition relation is nondeterministic; the restoration condition requires that on every computation path (or, in the standard definition, on every accepting path) the catalytic tape is returned to its initial content τ. The corresponding nondeterministic class is denoted NCL.

Problem. Exhibit a "genuinely nontrivial" use of nondeterminism in conjunction with catalytic computation. More precisely, one of the following:

(a) Give a computational task, a complexity-theoretic separation, or a structural result whose proof uses a nondeterministic catalytic algorithm in an essential way — i.e., a way that does not reduce immediately to either a standard deterministic catalytic simulation or to ordinary nondeterministic space, and that goes beyond the use of nondeterminism implicit in the definition of NCL.

(b) Equivalently, design a nondeterministic catalytic logspace algorithm for some language L such that the algorithm crucially exploits both the catalytic tape and the nondeterministic branching (for instance, by solving a problem not known to lie in CL via a guessing-and-verification strategy that maintains the catalyst), and prove its correctness and the catalyst-restoration property.

The task is to produce such an application, or to prove that no such nontrivial combination is possible (e.g., by showing NCL = CL via a simulation that renders nondeterminism inessential in this setting).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of nontrivially combining nondeterminism with catalytic computation is recognized as open in the catalytic-computation literature. Buhrman–Koucký–Loff–Speelman defined nondeterministic catalytic space and asked whether nondeterminism adds power. Recent work (2024–2025) has produced partial results — e.g., collapses showing that in some parameter regimes nondeterministic and randomized catalytic logspace coincide with CL — but no widely accepted "genuinely nontrivial" algorithmic use of nondeterminism within the catalytic model has been established. The question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic space: non-determinism and hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Studies nondeterministic catalytic space and raises questions about its power relative to deterministic catalytic space.
status_evidence.claim: Nondeterministic catalytic space is a defined model whose power relative to CL is studied but not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Unambiguous Catalytic Computation (FSTTCS 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates restricted forms of nondeterminism in catalytic computation; leaves the general question of nontrivial nondeterministic catalytic algorithms open.
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted (unambiguous) uses of nondeterminism in catalytic computation are known, with the general question open.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Logspace: Complexity & Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results show collapses between deterministic, nondeterministic and randomized catalytic logspace in certain regimes, suggesting nondeterminism may not add power.
status_evidence.claim: Partial collapse results indicate nondeterminism may be inessential in some regimes, but the broader question of nontrivial use is unresolved.
